answer: A shop agent auctions one mirror decorated with yarrow from a local forge using sealed bids: the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest bid. With an honest seller, binding bids and no bidder bonuses, a buyer cannot lower its price by adding aliases. Losing aliases can only raise the price paid by its winning account; if an alias wins, it still pays at least the highest rival bid. Thus extra buyer identities offer no gain in this single-item auction. Seller shill bidding remains a separate risk.
